analysis:
Examined all three BASE documentation units in docs/reference/configuration.md: placement and approval lifecycle (950–1127), privileged link repair and diagnostics (1228–1486), and configuration protection, batch/assistant policies and retirement (1487–1594), plus the bounded patch and complete changed-range map. Most supplied surrounding behavior is unchanged; existing launch-readiness fallback and network repair behavior are not PR findings. No concrete regression is established by these BASE excerpts and the partial documentation patch.
The patch introduces release-published cluster_runtime facts with pair-serving grants and parity qualifications, and describes coordinator-derived approvals. Integration must verify the changed release lane and coordinator acceptance contract: possession of A-005/release publication authority must not substitute for independently approved A-017 qualification or serving authorization (A-016, T-052/T-054/T-056). The supplied text establishes neither an authorization bypass nor how those gates interact. BASE approval checks at 1033–1041 and 1079–1127 bind installed files, policy, expiry and starts; changes to withdrawal and command-lock behavior at BASE 1039/1041 need HEAD evidence to validate preservation.
Assistant discovery and saved policy change at BASE 1568/1572–1573 also require HEAD/runtime evidence to check inventory binding, complete native capacity pricing, bilateral LOAD/READY agreement and request isolation (TB-007, A-001/A-018). No supplied change alters T-041's authenticated cache scope, HMAC storage, encryption or TTL. Detailed HEAD text and implementations were not supplied here; remaining release/qualification, approval-lifecycle and assistant questions should be reconciled in integration, not treated as proven vulnerabilities. Only selected canonical definitions were available in full.
